 SCCH - 25 2 MVC No. 2814/2023  JUDGMENT

The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries suffered by him in a road accident dated 30.03.2023.
2.

The case of the Petitioner in brief is that:
On 30.03.2023 at about 10.00am the petitioner was traveling as a passenger in the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 57-F-4510, coming from Mysore towards Chinya Bus Stop, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District.

When the petitioner was deboarding the Ramegowda vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157423559/
1
KSRTC bus at the Chinya Bus Stop, the driver of the KSRTC bus stopped and moved the bus suddenly even before the petitioner could get out completely without giving any indication.
The driver of the KSRTC bus drove the bus without ensuring the passenger has deboarded or not, thus causing the accident due to rash and negligent manner and also endangering human life.
As a result of KSRTC Bus Driver's negligence the petitioner fell down from the bus and suffered grievous injuries.

It is the further case of the Petitioner that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital Nagamangala, Mandya District, first aid treatment was given and then shifted to KIMS Hospital at Bangalore, where he was treated for 17 days and underwent operation and discharged with advice for follow up treatment and complete bed rest.

He has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/-
towards treatment, hospital charges, medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental expenses.
Prior to the date of accident he was hale and healthy, aged about 70 years, doing Coolie work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-57-F-4510.
The Nagamangala Rural Police have registered a case against the Driver of the Said bus in Cr.No.56/2023.
Hence the Respondent being the RC owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
this petition.
In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondent appeared and filed written statement.
5. The objections of the Respondent:
It has denied the averments of the petition.
It has denied the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the KSRTC Bus.

Further stated that on 30.03.2023 the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-4510 was proceeding from Mysore towards Tumkur, driven by its driver slowly, carefully on the left side of the Road observing all the traffic rules and regulations, when the said Bus proceeding slowly reached Chinya Village, Honakere Village at about 10.00 am and stationed the said bus at Bus Stop,
some of the passengers got down from the bus, among them one old person, aged about 70 years while getting down from the bus slipped from the steps of the bus, lost control over himself and fell down from the stationed bus to the Road, due to which he suffered injuries.
This accident occurred purely due to the negligence of old man.
The driver of the Bus was not at all responsible for the accident.
But the petitioner colluded with the SCCH - 25 5 MVC No. 2814/2023 jurisdictional police authority and filed a false case against the driver of the said KSRTC bus.
Further denied the age, avocation, income, medical expenses.

Further contended that the compensation Ramegowda vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157423559/
2 claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.

entities.text: Ramegowda vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:-
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 30.03.2023 at 10.00am., due to rash and negligent driving of driver of KSRTC bus bearing registration Number: KA-57-F-4510 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
7.
The Petitioner in order to prove his case, has examined himself as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.11.
Dr.Ramesh - Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore got examined as Pw.2 and got marked Exs.P.12 & SCCH - 25 6 MVC No. 2814/2023 13.
He also got examined Smt.Anupama - Medical Record Technician at KIMS hospital, Bangalore as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.14 to 17.

On the other side, the Respondent examined the Driver of the KSRTC Bus Mr.Kale Gowda as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1.
8.
Heard the arguments of the learned counsels for both the parties.

9. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows:-
 Issue No.1: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative,
 Issue No.3: As per the final order,
 for the following:-
 REASONS  10. Issue No.1:
In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the Driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57-F-4510, the petitioner has examined himself as PW.1 and has got marked 6 documents as per Exs.
P.1 to 6
. PW.1 has reiterated the averments of the SCCH - 25 7 MVC No. 2814/2023 petition in his affidavit in lieu of his chief examination.
In the cross-examination of PW.1, nothing worthwhile is elicited.

In support of his case he has also got examined the MRO of KIMS Hospital, Bangalore as PW.3 and got marked Exs.14 to 17 i.e.,
authorization letter, copy of police intimation, MLC register extract and case sheet.
During the cross examination of PW.3, nothing worthwhile is elicited.

The Respondent has contended that there was Ramegowda vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157423559/
3 negligence on the part of the petitioner.

entities.text: Ramegowda vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In support of the same, they got examined the Driver of KSRTC Bus as RW.1, who has reiterated the contentions in the written statement in his affidavit filed in lieu of his chief examination.
He got marked the Authorization letter as Ex.R.1.
During his cross-examination he has stated that the Bus left Mysore at 9.15am, it was supposed to reach Tumkur around 2.45 to 3.00pm.
The petitioner was passenger in the Bus.
After three people the petitioner alighted from the Bus.
He has not complained to the jurisdictional police, but informed to the Depot.
Further stated that there was no negligence on his SCCH - 25 8 MVC No. 2814/2023 part.
The chargesheet is filed against him and he has not challenged the same.

11. The accident took place on 30.03.2023 at 10.00am to 10.10am and the FIR at Ex.P.1 is registered on the very next day i.e., on 31.03.2023 at 12.15pm on the complaint of Mr.Lokesh son of the petitioner.
The Crime Details Form at Ex.P.2 gives the details of the accident.
As per Ex.P.3 wound certificate the accident occurred on 30.03.2023 at 11.30 am, due to which the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries.
The IMV report at Ex.P.4 shows that this accident was not due to any mechanical defects.
Ex.P.5 is notices to the RC owner of the offending vehicle and reply notice.
The police has field charge sheet after investigation as per Ex.P.6 against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Ex.P.15 i.e., intimation to police given by KIMS Hospital, Bangalore and Ex.16 MLC register extract from KIMS hospital.
All these documents show that the accident has occurred on the date and time as stated in the petition by the petitioner.
There is no contrary evidence by the respondent about this.

On the basis of document on SCCH - 25 9 MVC No. 2814/2023 record before the court it can be held that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the KSRTC Bus and there was no negligence of the petitioner in the case.
The respondent has not produced any document to show that there was negligence on the part of the Petitioner.
Hence, I hold that the accident occurred on 30.03.2023 and the petitioner suffered injuries in the accident.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:-
In order to prove the injuries and disability suffered by the petitioner, the petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.3.

As per Ex.P.3, the Petitioner has suffered - (1) Tenderness present over right thigh and (ii) Tenderness present over right hip region which are grievous in nature, diagnosed with traumatic inter trochasteric fracture of right femur.
13. PW.1 also got examined Dr.Ramesh B. as PW.2.

He has deposed the details of treatment undergone by the SCCH - 25 10 MVC No. 2814/2023 petitioner and has assessed the permanent physical disability of left lower limb at 30% and to the whole body at 15%.
He has got marked OPD Card and X-ray of petitioner as per Exs.P.12 & 13.
14 . During the cross examination of PW.2, has stated that he has not treated the petitioner, seen only discharge summary and wound certificate and the fractures are united, implants are in situ.

On perusal of the evidence of Pw.2 it is clear that the petitioner has suffered intertrochanteric fracture of right femur and is suffering from disability which has affected his mobility and stability.
The petitioner has averred that he was doing Coolie work.

Therefore, it is clear that the disability of his Ramegowda vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157423559/
4

entities.text: Ramegowda vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: right femur will affect his work and day today activities
. Accordingly, the court deems it fit to fix the functional disability at 10%.

Monthly income:
15.
The Petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, he was doing Coolie work and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
However he has not produced any document in support of the same, nor has he examined any witness.
The accident occurred in the year 2023.

Therefore, this court deems it fit to fix the notional income of the petitioner is Rs.16,000/- per month.
16.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 74 years as could be made out from Ex.P.11/Notarized copy of Aadhar Card.
He was hale and healthy before the accident.

Keeping all the above things in mind, Petitioner is entitled to the following compensation:-
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:-

After the accident, the Petitioner was treated at Govt. Hospital, Nagamangala, Manyda District, after first aid treatment he was shifted to KIMS Hospital, admitted as an inpatient from 30.03.2023 to 03.04.2023, operated and discharged with advice.
In this regard, he has produced Ex.P.7 Discharge summary issued by KIMS Hospital and Research Center.
Considering that the injuries he has undergone are SCCH - 25 12 MVC No. 2814/2023 grievous and considering his age, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.
ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The Petitioner has pleaded that he has spent a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- towards hospitalization,
medical expenses, extra nourishment, conveyance and other miscellaneous expenses etc.,
In this regard, he has produced medical bills as per Ex.P.8 for a sum of Rs.54,090/-.
There is no contrary evidence to these bills from the respondent.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under this head.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:-
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injury.
The petitioner has taken treatment for almost 5 days at KIMS Hospital & Research Centre, Bangalore as can be made out from Ex.P.7 Discharge summary.

Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner may have required at least One month time SCCH - 25 13 MVC No. 2814/2023 for recovering from the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.16,000/- under this head.

iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:-
Ramegowda vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157423559/
5

sentences.text: On perusal of Ex.P.11, as on the date of accident he was 74 years old.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable for his age is 5.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.96,000/- (Rs.16,000/- x 12 x 5 x 10%=
Rs.96,000/-) under this head.

(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND  HAPPINESS:-
The Petitioner was aged about 74 years at the time of accident.
He has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal, he is suffering from 10% functional disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout his life.
Moreover he will always feel that he cannot do his normal activities as previous to the date of accident.
Because of this he will have to lose some of the amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries SCCH - 25 14 MVC No. 2814/2023 that the Petitioner has suffered, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under this head.
(vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:
After the accident, the Petitioner was treated in the above said hospitals, admitted for 5 days as an inpatient and discharged with advise.
However, during this period he must have spent considerable amount on his food and nourishment, conveyance and attendant expenses.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/-
under this head.
(vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the version of PW.3, the Petitioner has to undergo another surgery for removal of implants.
In this regard the petitioner or the PW.2 have not produced any estimation bills.

Therefore, looking at the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and the evidence on record, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.

The Petitioner is entitled to compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.1,00,000/-
2. Medical expenses Rs.54,090/-
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.16,000/- period Ramegowda vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157423559/
6 4.

Loss of future income Rs.96,000/-
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.20,000/- happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/- nourishment charges 7.

Future Medical Expenses Rs.20,000/-
TOTAL Rs.3,26,090/-
If it is rounded off it comes around Rs.3,26,100/- and same is awarded under different heads to the Petitioner.
LIABILITY 18.
The respondent contended that the negligence was on the part of the petitioner himself, has failed to prove the same.
Therefore, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.15,00,000/- but he is entitled only for a sum of SCCH - 25 16 MVC No. 2814/2023 Rs.3,26,100/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
19. Issue No.3:

For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this court proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,26,100/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Twenty Six Thousand and One Hundred only)
from the Respondent along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondent is liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
The Respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this SCCH - 25 17 MVC No. 2814/2023 Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.

from the Respondent along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondent is liable to pay the said compensation to the petitioner.
The Respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this SCCH - 25 17 MVC No. 2814/2023 Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of e-payment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw decree accordingly.
